quote: Example 3.5. As an application of the previous results, choose as baseline the standard exponential distribution E(x) = 1 − e^{−x}, for x ≥ 0, and, for β > 0, T(β, E)(x) = 1 − (1 − E(x))^β = 1 − e^{−βx}, the exponential distribution with hazard rate β. Then, with the notation of Theorems 3.1 and 3.3, X = (X1, . . . , Xn) and Y = (Y1, . . . , Yn) are random vectors with dependent components whose marginal distributions are heterogeneous exponentials. Assume the distributions of X and Y are described using a Clayton copula with parameters γ1 and γ2, respectively, such that γ2 ≥ γ1 > 0. Then, as referred in Example 2.6, ϕ2 ◦ ψ1 is super-additive. Hence, from Theorem 3.1, if αi ≤ βi, i = 1, . . . , n, it follows that Xn:n(α) ≥st Yn:n(β). In case we do not have increasing coordinates for the parameter vectors, but they still satisfy α ⪰^m β, we get a conclusion using Theorem 3.3. Moreover, for the Clayton generator ψ2' ◦ ϕ2(T(β, E))(x) = −(1 − e^{−x})^{1+γ2}, so V(β) = −x(1 − e^{−βx})^{−(1+γ2)} e^{−βx}, which is increasing with respect to β > 0, so again we conclude that Xn:n(α) ≥st Yn:n(β).

quote: Example 3.17. Take E(x) = 1 − e^{−x}, for x ≥ 0, the standard exponential, and the functional T(α, E)(x) = 1 − (1 − E(x))^α = 1 − e^{−αx}, where α > 0. Consider a system with n = 3 components with lifetimes T(αi, E), for i = 1, 2, 3, whose joint distribution is described by an Archimedean copula with Clayton generator ψ(t) = (1 + t)^{−1}, for t ≥ 0. With α = (α1, α2, α3), the lifetime of a 2-out-of-3 system is X2:3(α), whose distribution function is obtained by using (12): F^(α)_2:3(x) = ψ(t1 + t2) + ψ(t1 + t3) + ψ(t2 + t3) − 2ψ(t1 + t2 + t3), where ti = (e^{αi x} − 1)^{−1}. A direct differentiation with respect to αℓ gives ∂F^(α)_2:3/∂αℓ(x) = t'ℓ (Σ_{j≠ℓ} ψ'(tℓ + tj) − 2ψ'(t1 + t2 + t3)), where t'ℓ = −xe^{αℓ x}(e^{αℓ x} − 1)^{−2}. Choosing now α = (1, 2.5, 4), the plots for (αℓ − αm)(∂F^(α)_2:3/∂αℓ − ∂F^(α)_2:3/∂αm) are shown in Figure 1. Although when taking (ℓ, m) = (1, 3) or (2, 3) the curve has a constant sign, the case (ℓ, m) = (1, 2) changes sign as x ranges (0, +∞). Hence, the map α ↦ F^(α)_2:3(x) is neither Schur-convex nor Schur-concave.
